note: Pre-registration only means something if it predates the measurement. Several hypotheses in hypotheses.jsonl were already observed during the build, so registering them now would be backdating, and they are listed under `exploratory_by_construction` instead. Only genuinely untested claims are registered as confirmatory. The referee reads the `claims` list; everything else here is documentation for a reader.

claims.statement: The CC2 label-budget plateau for delta-learning on E1 occurs at a LARGER number of labels under scaffold shift than under a random split.
claims.primary_outcome: smallest n_train whose validation MAE is within 10% of the fully-trained delta MAE, compared between the random and scaffold splits
claims.mechanism: If delta-learning fits a smooth local correction to the cheap surface, a shifted test distribution should need materially more labels to reach the same error.
claims.falsified_if: The two curves plateau at the same label count, which would mean the correction is more global than assumed -- a claim about the physics rather than the model.

claims.statement: Molecules whose excited states are misordered between TDDFT and CC2 are separable from the rest using structure-derived features alone.
claims.primary_outcome: ratio of delta-model MAE between the highest and lowest quartile of a structure-only predictor of misordering, with a paired bootstrap interval
claims.mechanism: Ordering ambiguity concentrates in near-degenerate states, and near-degeneracy has structural correlates a fingerprint can represent.
claims.falsified_if: No structure-only slice separates the swapped population beyond the paired bootstrap interval.

claims.statement: A frontier model driving this same harness will explore the METHOD axis in at least 6 of 8 seeds, and reach a best E1 within 20% of the fixed grid's 0.06446 eV.
claims.primary_outcome: (a) count of seeds whose experiment log contains at least one method='delta' run, out of 8; (b) mean best-found E1 validation MAE across 8 seeds
claims.mechanism: Qwen3 8B fixated on method='direct' in 5 of 8 seeds and never varied the one axis that matters, so its failure is confounded with capacity. If a stronger model explores the axis, capacity was the constraint. If it also fixates, the constraint is the harness -- the tool schema and system prompt -- which is actionable.
claims.falsified_if: Fewer than 6 of 8 seeds try delta, or mean best E1 exceeds 0.07735. Either outcome is reported; a null here is the more useful finding.
claims.note: Registered before any frontier-model API key was available to this project, so no result could have informed it.

exploratory_by_construction.why: Measured (0.0630 vs 0.0721 eV, CI [-0.011,-0.007]) before any registration existed. The result stands; its status does not.
Observed during the build via slice_error, then re-measured on the sealed set (2.26x, CI [1.97,2.59]). Registering it now would be backdating.
The three cheap levels were swept during the state-ordering analysis before this file existed.
exploratory_by_construction.status: partially falsified -- swap RATE falls with baseline quality (16.4% SVP > 12.1% TZVP > 11.8% CAM) exactly as predicted, but oracle GAIN does not (19.7%, 14.8%, 20.8%). The mechanism holds for how often states are misordered; it does not hold for how much that costs.

exploratory_by_construction.status: FALSIFIED and withdrawn from the write-up

agent_claims.note: Claims produced by agent rollouts are exploratory by definition -- the agent chooses what to claim after seeing validation results, which is the adaptive selection pre-registration exists to prevent. They are audited on the sealed set and reported with their multiplicity, never as confirmatory.
agent_claims.superseded: Two earlier figures are NOT reproducible and are recorded only so the drift is visible: a 3-seed audit reported 2 signed / 1 rejected, and an 8-seed audit reported 1 signed / 2 narrowed / 5 rejected. The trace files behind both are gone. The current line is from clean hash-bound traces; two verdicts moved because of referee bugs (split inference, and set-equality scoping that penalised extra evidence), not agent merit.
